title: Aria-friendly palette anchors and proportional gap matrix
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Summary: Refresh core design tokens to introduce ARIA-friendly color anchors, a proportional gap/radius matrix, and a micro-shadow ramp for improved legibility and composability across buttons, tables, and charts. This ticket covers the token definitions, rationale, implementation guidance, migration strategy, and rollout plan.

Background: Our current token set has drifted toward many ad-hoc surface colors and shadow presets. Teams report inconsistent contrast in dense tables and small controls, and engineering has requested clearer rules for radius scaling across responsive breakpoints. The goal is to consolidate tokens into a small, opinionated set that: (1) meets WCAG AA/AAA where practical, (2) maps cleanly to component states, (3) supports a high-contrast accessibility mode, and (4) reduces cognitive overhead for implementers.

Goals: 
- Define 10 color anchors (semantic + neutral) with token names and contrast targets against both white and 800-gray backgrounds.
- Introduce a proportional gap matrix (4, 8, 12, 16, 24, 32) and explicit radius scale variants (none, micro, standard, pill) with breakpoint guidance.
- Create a 6-step micro-shadow/elevation ramp optimized for small elements (buttons, table rows, chart overlays) with physical-like penumbra and ambient components.
- Provide migration guidance and codemods for button, table, and chart components.
- Add acceptance criteria and testing checklist for accessibility and visual regressions.

Design decisions and trade-offs: 
- Contrast prioritization: We target AA for body text and UI labels, AAA for primary action text where possible. For tertiary UI accents we accept AA minima but provide explicit high-contrast overrides. This favors legibility over maximal visual subtlety.
- Palette anchors instead of infinite swatches: We create anchored token values (neutral-100..900, accent-500, success-600, warn-500, danger-600) and forbid per-component custom colors unless reviewed. This reduces variance at the cost of slightly less visual expressiveness for product teams.
- Radius proportionality: radii scale with container density (dense / default / loose). For example, a table cell in dense mode uses micro radius (2px) while cards use standard (8px). This trades one-size-fits-all simplicity for better visual coherence in dense UIs.
- Shadow clarity: We flatten multi-layer shadows into a compact micro-ramp to avoid heavy, platform-specific blur artifacts. Shadows will have named tokens like shadow-01..shadow-06 with explicit rgba strings tied to light/dark themes.

Acceptance criteria: 
- Token file (JSON + CSS variables) merged to tokens repo with tests passing.
- Figma library updated with token variants and component instances for primary button, table row, chart tooltip.
- Accessibility report demonstrating contrast ratios for anchor tokens against default and high-contrast backgrounds (reports attached).
- Migration guide and codemod PR created for the button package and tables package.
- Two-week canary rollout plan documented and scheduled with Platform team.

Implementation notes for engineers: 
- Token naming convention: semantic-first, then scale. Examples: color-bg-primary, color-text-body, color-border-weak, radius-standard, gap-16, shadow-03.
- Export formats: tokens.json (source of truth), CSS custom properties (for hosted), tokens.ts for JS usage, and SCSS variables for legacy packages.
- The shadow ramp intentionally uses lower alpha values and smaller y-offsets for mobile to avoid perceived heaviness on small screens.

Migration plan: 
- Phase 1 (Canary): Replace tokens in Button package and small set of internal widgets (rollout to 3 product teams). Run visual diffs and accessibility checks.
- Phase 2: Migrate Table and Charts packages. Introduce density flags to enable proportional radius and gap matrices.
- Phase 3: Global rollout with codemods and deprecation warnings in console for legacy token names.

QA checklist: 
- Visual diff for primary, secondary, and tertiary buttons across breakpoints.
- Ensure table row height and vertical rhythm remain consistent for dense and default modes.
- Validate chart tooltip contrast and shadow visibility at 75% and 100% zoom.
- Run Lighthouse accessibility checks and internal contrast audit tool.

References and artifacts: 
- Figma: https://www.figma.com/file/EN9pwXkY/design-tokens-aria-anchors (library page)
- Confluence PRD: https://redwood.atlassian.net/wiki/spaces/DEV/pages/246810/Aria+Anchors+Token+Revamp
- GitHub PRs: https://github.com/redwood-inference/design-tokens/pull/412 (tokens), https://github.com/redwood-inference/components/pull/780 (button migration codemod)
- Accessibility report CSV: https://drive.google.com/file/d/1a2b3c4d5e6f-report

Follow-ups: 
- Create a small sample app that toggles density and high-contrast mode for demo and usability testing.
- Add unit tests to ensure CSS custom properties map to token values in runtime bundles.
comments: 2026-03-02 — Aisha Patel: Initial draft of anchors and gap matrix uploaded to Figma. I invited engineering and accessibility to comment. Key decision: prioritize AA for body text; plan for a high-contrast override.
2026-03-04 — Benji O'Connor (Eng): Reviewed token export formats. Requested tokens.ts export with typed token names to reduce runtime errors. Action: Marco will add typed exports in PR.

2026-03-06 — Priya Singh (Accessibility): Flagged color-accent-400 vs neutral-800 for chart labels; recommended shifting accent-400 darker by ~6% to meet AA at small sizes. Updated palette proposal attached.

2026-03-08 — Marco Rivera (Assignee): Implemented initial tokens.json and CSS var output; opened GH PR #412. Noted that shadow-05 produced heavy rendering on Android; adjusted alpha values for mobile form factor in tokens-mobile.json.

2026-03-10 — Lina Chen (PM): Reviewed migration plan. Requested explicit fallback guidance for third-party charts that accept color strings. Added step to surface a console migration checklist for apps using ChartJS/D3.

2026-03-12 — Design review: Team asked to add examples of density transitions in Figma (dense -> default) and a note on how radius scales should animate (scale vs instant). Added micro-prototype frames.

2026-03-14 — Visual QA: Ran snapshot diffs for Button package (desktop + mobile). Two regressions found in ghost-button hover shadow; label assigned to ENG-81233 for follow-up. Can proceed to canary after fix.
2026-03-15 — Aisha Patel: Updated PR descriptions and added the accessibility CSV report. Requesting final sign-off from accessibility and eng infra to schedule canary deployment on 2026-03-22.
notes: This ticket is intentionally prescriptive about token naming to simplify runtime feature flags. Teams that need expressive palettes should request exception via product review.
demo_request: Please schedule a 30-minute demo with Growth and Platform teams in the week after canary (target week 2026-03-29).
